Timeline::add_years¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::add_years(int years) const

Shift By Calendar Years¶

add_years() moves every defined instant by an integer number of years on the calendar displayed by the Timeline. It exists for rules stated in years: anniversary dates, annual review points, and the same local appointment in a later or earlier year.

This is calendar arithmetic, not multiplication by 365 days. The method first reads each instant as local year, month, day, and clock fields in tz(), changes the year, and resolves those fields back to an instant. Consequently it keeps the local month, day, time of day, and nanosecond whenever that date exists.

Use add_years(n) when same calendar position, n years away is the rule. Use add_duration when the rule is a fixed elapsed interval.

Leap-Day Rule¶

A leap-day anniversary may land in a year without February 29. In that one case, add_years() clamps the day to the final valid day of the destination month. Thus February 29 becomes February 28; it does not spill into March. Other valid month/day pairs retain their day exactly.

Example 1. Shift a leap day and ordinary dates forward one year. The 2-D shape and every subsecond field are retained.

const auto calendar = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-02-29T08:15:30.123456789Z", "2023-01-31T23:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-03-31T12:00:00Z", "2024-12-31T23:59:59.999999999Z"},
});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    calendar.add_years(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2025-02-28T08:15:30.123456789+00:00", "2024-01-31T23:00:00.000000000+00:00"], 
  ["2025-03-31T12:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2025-12-31T23:59:59.999999999+00:00"]
]

Direction And Zero¶

years is signed. Positive values move toward later calendar years, negative values move toward earlier years, and zero reconstructs the same local fields. The operation is out of place: it returns a new Timeline and never rewrites the receiver.

Example 2. A negative count applies the same leap-day clamp in the earlier year.

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    calendar.add_years(-1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2023-02-28T08:15:30.123456789+00:00", "2022-01-31T23:00:00.000000000+00:00"], 
  ["2023-03-31T12:00:00.000000000+00:00", "2023-12-31T23:59:59.999999999+00:00"]
]

Example 3. A zero shift leaves the value unchanged; the separate source print also demonstrates that a nonzero shift does not mutate its receiver.

const auto source = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T08:15:30.123456789Z");
const auto shifted = source.add_years(1);
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    source.add_years(0), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    source, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-02-29T08:15:30.123456789+00:00"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-02-29T08:15:30.123456789+00:00"

Shape, Timezone, And Absent Instants¶

The scalar count applies elementwise to any rank. The output has the receiver’s shape and timezone label, including for non-contiguous borrowed storage. Defined values are read through logical strides. NaT remains NaT, and an empty input returns an empty output with the same shape.

Example 4. Leap-day clamping also works through a stride-two borrowed view; the padding elements are not mistaken for timestamps.

std::array<std::int64_t, 4> backing{
    1'704'067'200'123'456'789LL, 111LL,
    1'709'164'800'000'000'004LL, 222LL};
const std::array<std::int64_t, 1> shape{2};
const std::array<std::int64_t, 1> strides{2};
const auto strided = pluss::Timeline::from_buffer(
    backing.data(), shape, strides, {}, "UTC");

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    strided.add_years(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["2025-01-01T00:00:00.123456789+00:00", "2025-02-28T00:00:00.000000004+00:00"]

Failure Conditions¶

The destination must be representable by the supported civil calendar and by the signed 64-bit epoch-nanosecond storage. The method rejects an out-of-range year and rejects a reconstructed local wall time that does not exist in the timeline’s timezone. It never returns a partially shifted result.

Example 5. Advancing beyond the calendar range is rejected.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeline::make("9999-12-31T00:00:00Z").add_years(1);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected
